question: Who among the following is not one of the 3 most important gods mentioned in the Rig Veda?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Prajapati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rig Veda, one of the oldest sacred texts of India, primarily mentions three principal deities: Agni, Indra, and Soma.
 
• Agni, the fire god, is considered a mediator between the gods and humans, and is invoked in numerous hymns.
 
• Indra, the king of gods, is celebrated as a warrior deity who combats demons and is associated with rain and thunderstorms.
 
• Soma, both a deity and a ritual drink, is venerated for its invigorating properties and is central to various Rigvedic hymns.
 
• Prajapati, although important in later Vedic literature, does not hold a primary position in the Rig Veda.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agni**

 
 
• Agni is depicted as a divine messenger who conveys offerings to the gods.
 
• He is associated with the sacrificial fire and is invoked in the initiation of Vedic rituals.
 
 
 
• **Indra**
 
 
• Indra's exploits, such as slaying the serpent Vritra, are extensively narrated in the Rig Veda.
 
• He is often depicted riding a white elephant named Airavata.
 
 
 
• **Soma**
 
 
• Soma is both a plant and the extracted juice used in Vedic rituals.
 
• It is considered to confer immortality and divine inspiration.
 
 
 
• **Prajapati**
 
 
• Prajapati means "Lord of Creatures" and is associated with creation and procreation.
 
• His prominence increases in the later Vedic texts and Upanishads.
